solution.what: Tomokiyo nevers.htm and the DECODE record checked for a decipherment of R4176.
DECODE R4176 images P1-P14 downloaded with the session cookie.
Tomokiyo's Nevers cipher no. 35, described as used by the Duke of Mantua in 1590, traced to BnF fr. 3995 f. 64 'Per Cavare 1590' (Gallica btv1b525085665 canvas 131) and read.
Unseparated two-digit figures transcribed from the images: f. 92r in the main session, ff. 92v and 93r by two subagents.
Key applied unchanged; Italian reads at once on f. 92r (la morte del Papa sia stata procurata con veleno da Spagnoli).
Beam decoder with the it-cinquecento LM resolving 3/9 and 0/8 look-alikes, then 7/8 added; f. 93r reads through.
Sign and title values (che, per, et, S. M.ta, Legato, Monsignor ...) read from the key sheet and substituted.
Retry pass: a subagent re-read the doubtful lines at 3x; about 829 of 945 tokens now read (88%); garbled stretches on f. 92r and f. 93r and three signs absent from the key remain.

Blind re-transcription at 4x of every unread stretch by a subagent that had not seen ct_*.txt (blind_92r.md, blind_93r.md), compared with the old digits and decoded with beam.py/beam2.py: read contro cotesto Regno di Francia, buoni Italiani, anichilata, si vede, far riverenza, in quello; sottoporsi confirmed as written; +56 tokens; 92r l5 tail, l8 middle, 93r l4/l5/l8 and 92v stretch still do not read.

Second independent image: BnF microfilm on Gallica (btv1b9060544v, canvases 160-162) used to re-read every unread stretch. f. 93r l4 q-like sign = key's non, ● = che, 'si come non ho mancato in quello che'; l5 14 35 31 38 'hora'. 92r l5 tail, 92r l8 middle, 92v 'la mondeza a me' and 93r l8 code group match the DECODE digits and stay unread. Measured 878 of 923 tokens (95.1%).
Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): the three page transcriptions ct_92r/ct_92v/ct_93r and the reading reading.md (clear and deciphered text together)

Read share recounted over cipher words only (README Conventions, 16 Nov 2026). The cipher is the bold passages of reading.md; the nested bold round 'non hò mancato' and 'sin hora' on f. 93r was read as one cipher passage. Holes were counted by words, and the four unread stretches were sized from their letter counts (2, 6, 1, 1 words; an estimate). Nulls are not holes, and the hole after 'di Monsignor' is in the clear. Result: 212 read, 12 unread, 0.946 (was 0.991, measured over the whole file with the clear text). The letter goes from read to read in part, and so does the class; fraction_read (878 of 923 tokens) is unchanged.

Gonzaga recount revised to the README sizing rule (a hole mark covers the least number of words the decode shows, an estimate). Letter runs were sized at one word per 13 letters (the longest cipher word read here), and a code word counts as a word on its own: unread stretches 1, 4, 1 and 1 words, plus 2 part-words. Result: 9 unread of 221 cipher words, 0.959 >= 0.95. The letter and the class go back to read. The mean-length sizing (4.6 letters a word) gave 0.946 and is withdrawn as the measure.

texts.label: BnF fr. 3979 ff. 92-93, Vincenzo Gonzaga to Nevers, Mantua, 17 Sept 1590
texts.summary: Vincenzo I Gonzaga, Duke of Mantua, writes to his uncle Louis de Gonzague, duc de Nevers: he reports the rumour that Sixtus V was poisoned by the Spaniards, welcomes Henri IV's expected conversion, and assures Nevers (for the King) of his devotion to the French crown against the 'common enemy', a guarded pro-Bourbon declaration of September 1590. Deciphered with Nevers cipher no. 35 (BnF fr. 3995 f. 64).
texts.note: 16 Nov 2026 (revised the same day): read share over cipher words only 0.959. That is 212 cipher words read and 9 unread, counted in the bold (deciphered) passages of reading.md. Holes are counted by words, with each unread stretch at the least number of words its decode allows (README, an estimate). A letter run counts at least one word per 13 letters, 13 being the longest cipher word read in this letter, and a code word counts as a word on its own. That gives: 92r l5 tail, 10 letters, 1 word; 92r l8 middle, 24 letters + the code 26 Inglesi + 2 letters, 4 words; 92v, 6 letters, 1 word; the 93r l8 code group, 1 word. The part-words c[..] and per[?] add 1 each. The nulls {0Δ}, {4-sign}, {9} are not holes, and the [..] after 'di Monsignor' is in the clear. Stays read. At 4.6 letters a word (the mean of the read cipher), the first count of the day, it would be 0.946 (12 unread); with bare marks, 0.968. Whole letter, clear included, not the measure: 0.991.
